translatorNotes: Register: informal tú, consistent with Phase 1.

'TMS' kept (Transport Management System; standard acronym in ES logistics). 'ETA' kept, glossed once as 'hora estimada de llegada (ETA)'. 'POD' (Proof of Delivery) rendered as 'comprobante de entrega (POD)' first use, then 'comprobante de entrega'.

'shipment' -> 'envío'; 'load' (freight) -> 'carga'; 'dispatch/dispatchers' -> 'central/operadores' (dispatch office = 'central', dispatcher = 'operador'); 'carrier' -> 'transportista'; 'check in/check calls' -> 'registro/llamadas de control'; 'dock appointment' -> 'cita de muelle'; 'detention' -> 'detención' (freight detention). FLAG: 'central'/'operador' vs 'centro de control'/'despachador' varies by market (Spain vs LatAm trucking) — reviewer to confirm.
'where is my shipment' -> '¿dónde está mi envío?'; the ecommerce cross-reference 'where is my order' -> '¿dónde está mi pedido?' (matches ecommerce page).
'3PL' glossed as 'operadores logísticos (3PL)'. 'freight broker' -> 'agente de carga'. 'courier and delivery' -> 'mensajería y reparto'.
Stat chip data-prefix 'under ' -> 'menos de ' and suffix ' sec' -> ' seg'; '20+ hrs' -> '20+ h'; '24/7' unchanged.
Prices/figures unchanged, currency named: '$1,000 and $5,000' -> '1.000 y 5.000 dólares'; '$50 to $300' -> '50 a 300 dólares'. '$11k' kept as-is in the case-study chip (compact display).
Case study reuses the ecommerce WISMO story deliberately (source does too, as an adjacent-industry analogy); kept faithful.
Brand names (Twilio, WhatsApp Business, n8n, Make, Google Workspace, Slack) unchanged.
Blog 'related reading' links point to English blog posts (Phase 3 not started); anchor text translated. Nav/footer service + industry links point to /es.
